title: Reading Food in Layers
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Sort fourteen foods found in Istanbul into five historical layers: ancient Mediterranean and Anatolia, Turkic herders, Ottoman trade and court, the Americas after 1492, and the Turkish Republic.

learningObjectives: Classify fourteen foods found in Istanbul by the historical layer they came from, with at least 11 of 14 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The Turkic herders' arrival in Anatolia after 1071

keyQuestions: When did this food arrive on Istanbul's table?
Where did it first grow, and who brought it?
What does the food's name tell us?
commonMisconceptions: Tomatoes and peppers have always been part of Mediterranean cooking.
Tea is an ancient Ottoman drink.
Turkish cooking is essentially the same as Arab cooking.
Everything on a Turkish table came with the Turks from Central Asia.
Coffee was always part of life in Istanbul.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on fourteen cards (mastery: 11 of 14).
Name the layer of each part of menemen.
Explain what the word mısır reveals about corn.
